audits.title: Dental audit (I): Exact criteria of dental records; results of a Phase-III study.
audits.standard: 46 explicit criteria for completion of dental records
audits.setting: Faculty of Dentistry, University of Seville

cycle1.result: No record free from errors; maximum 36 of 46 criteria fulfilled (mean 20.8); the standard of appropriate completion was met in only 12 criteria (75%).

audits.intervention: Remedial action proposed (Phase IV): new model of dental record with re-evaluation (Phase V) in a second paper.
audits.other_findings: Deficiencies were greatest for diagnosis and treatment plan items.
audits.citation: Martín García P, Ríos Santos JV, Segura Egea JJ, Fernández Palacín A, Bullón Fernández P. Dental audit (I): Exact criteria of dental records; results of a Phase-III study. Med Oral Patol Oral Cir Bucal. 2008;13(7):E407-13. PMID: 18587303.

audits.title: Audit of dental reports (II): first Phase-II study in a Spanish Faculty of Dentistry.
audits.standard: 46 quality criteria for dental records; standard 75% completion per criterion
audits.setting: Comprehensive Dentistry Clinic, Faculty of Dentistry, University of Seville

cycle2.result: Standard of 75% reached in 29 criteria; fulfilment improved in 41 criteria, significantly in 25.

audits.other_findings: Follow-up of an earlier audit (Phase III, 50 records).
audits.citation: Ríos Santos JV, Martín García P, Segura Egea JJ, Fernández-Palacín A, Bullón Fernández P. Audit of dental reports (II): first Phase-II study in a Spanish Faculty of Dentistry. Med Oral Patol Oral Cir Bucal. 2008;13(8):E529-35. PMID: 18667990.

audits.title: Audit of dental practice record-keeping: a PCT-coordinated clinical audit by Worcestershire dentists.
audits.standard: Common framework of eight record-keeping domains; standard of grade 1 (good) or 2 (adequate)
audits.setting: NHS general dental practices, Worcestershire Primary Care Trust (collaborative audit)

cycle1.result: 161 of 184 dentists (87.5%) each audited 30 records. Proportion below standard: soft tissues 36%, periodontal status 30%, radiographic review 27%, note-taking 25%.

audits.intervention: PCT arranged postgraduate education on record keeping and raised awareness; individual anonymised peer comparison fed back
audits.other_findings: Wide variation between dentists in record keeping.
audits.citation: Cole A, McMichael A. Audit of dental practice record-keeping: a PCT-coordinated clinical audit by Worcestershire dentists. Prim Dent Care. 2009;16(3):85-93. doi:10.1308/135576109788634296. PMID: 19566980.

audits.title: Improving the quality of endodontic record keeping through clinical audit.
audits.setting: Restorative dentistry department, Morriston Hospital, Swansea, and an endodontic MSc course

cycle1.result: 50 departmental and 10 student record sets; most often missing were consent, anaesthetic details, rubber dam method, working length reference point, irrigation details and obturation technique.

audits.intervention: Presentation of results with an educational session; departmental guidelines, consent leaflets and endodontic record keeping forms.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in 24 of 29 areas in the departmental audit and 14 of 29 in the MSc audit (P = 0.05); some areas reached 100% when forms were used.

audits.citation: King E, Shekaran L, Muthukrishnan A. Improving the quality of endodontic record keeping through clinical audit. Br Dent J. 2017;222(5):373-380. doi:10.1038/sj.bdj.2017.223. PMID: 28281608.

audits.title: Inaccurate Dental Charting in an Audit of 1128 General Dental Practice Records.
audits.standard: GDC requirement for complete and accurate dental records

cycle1.result: 44% of dental charts were inaccurate (range 16% to 83% between practices); 13% missed amalgam and 18% missed tooth-coloured restorations.

audits.other_findings: 7.5% had amalgams charted that were not present; 5% had too many and 5% too few teeth charted.
audits.citation: Brown NL, Jephcote VEL. Inaccurate Dental Charting in an Audit of 1128 General Dental Practice Records. Dent Update. 2017;44(3):254-6, 259-60. doi:10.12968/denu.2017.44.3.254. PMID: 29172337.

audits.title: Evaluation of Record Keeping in Exodontia Department of Punjab Dental Hospital, Lahore: A Clinical Audit.
audits.setting: Exodontia department, Punjab Dental Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Most omitted: patient complaint, medical history and supervisor signatures.

audits.intervention: Results shared with students and a teaching session on record keeping.

cycle2.result: Compliance improved for all components except medical history and date.

audits.citation: Bin Zahid O, Rehman A, Shoaib M, Bilal M, Shaheen A, Jamil MH, et al.. Evaluation of Record Keeping in Exodontia Department of Punjab Dental Hospital, Lahore: A Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2023;15(1):e33645. doi:10.7759/cureus.33645. PMID: 36788907.

audits.title: Orthodontic Treatment Documentation by Postgraduate Students: A Comprehensive Audit and Peer Review.
audits.standard: Audit checklist adapted from available standards and guidelines (examination and diagnosis form criteria and treatment progress record attributes)
audits.setting: Orthodontic postgraduate clinic, Faculty of Dentistry, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia

cycle1.result: 80 (72.7%) records fully documented; radiographic findings and supervisor signatures frequently missing.

audits.other_findings: 64.5% of patients had non-attendance exceeding 8 weeks, strongly correlated with longer treatment times (r = 0.744).
audits.citation: Tan XY, Lau KL, Dino J, Syed Mohamed AMF, Ashari A, Ahmad N, et al.. Orthodontic Treatment Documentation by Postgraduate Students: A Comprehensive Audit and Peer Review. Eur J Dent Educ. 2026. doi:10.1111/eje.70139. PMID: 41873015.
